findings.issue: The test is named 'exactly one ForwardedHeaderFilter registration under the framework strategy', but oneRegistration() loads only ForwardedHeaderConfig and no Boot auto-configuration. The count would be 1 even if Boot's own registration stopped backing off after an upgrade. What the test proves is the @ConditionalOnProperty, which is still worth having. The back-off still rests on the CEO's reading of the Boot 4.0.7 source. The test also does not check the type of the registered filter.
findings.fix: Optionally add .withConfiguration(AutoConfigurations.of(<Boot's servlet web server / Tomcat auto-config that registers the forwarded filter>)) and assert getFilter() is a PeerRemoteAddressForwardedHeaderFilter. Otherwise rename the test so it describes the conditional only.

findings.issue: No test checks the dispatcher types (REQUEST, ASYNC, ERROR) or that customizers are applied. Both match Boot's registration on inspection, but a regression there would not fail the build.
findings.fix: Optional: in the context-runner test, assert the registration's dispatcher types, and that a stub ForwardedHeaderFilterCustomizer bean is invoked.

findings.issue: Helm now always sets SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none for user-service. Spring binds that env var with higher precedence than application.yml, so USER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY has no effect on Kubernetes. The resulting value (none) is the same and safe, but the documented knob is dead under Helm.
findings.fix: Optional: add a note to the USER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY doc row that Helm pins the server-level value, or drop the service-specific variable later.

summary: Delta 690f934a..a04ad610. Filter correctness: PeerRemoteAddressForwardedHeaderFilter reads getRemoteAddr/getRemoteHost/getRemotePort from the incoming request before calling super.doFilterInternal. It then wraps whatever request Spring's filter passes down (the ForwardedHeaderExtractingRequest) in PeerRemote, which returns those captured values. The forwarded host, proto, port and prefix overrides on the inner wrapper still apply, while X-Forwarded-For and RFC 7239 Forwarded: for= can no longer reach the remote address. Requests with no forwarded headers skip doFilterInternal through shouldNotFilter and keep the socket peer anyway. ERROR dispatch goes through doFilterNestedErrorDispatch, which calls the overridden doFilterInternal, so it is covered too. @ConditionalOnProperty(server.forward-headers-strategy=framework) matches Boot's own condition. setDispatcherTypes(REQUEST, ASYNC, ERROR) and customizers.orderedStream() match Boot's registration. Tests: peerWinsHostProtoKept covers mixed-case XFF, Forwarded for= (including an IPv6 value with a port, mixed case) and both headers together. It asserts addr, host, port and ClientIp, and separately asserts that server name and scheme are still taken from the forwarded headers. Removing PeerRemote fails the Forwarded cases, breaking host/proto fails the last asserts, and dropping the conditional fails the strategy=none runner. The context test does not prove that Boot backs off (nit). Helm: every service except auth now gets SERVER_FORWARD_HEADERS_STRATEGY=none. Auth gets framework only from values.yaml:140, so no env entry is duplicated. A grep of the non-auth services' main sources finds no URL building from the request (fromCurrentRequest, getRequestURL, sendRedirect, isSecure) and no request-based cookie Secure logic. All redirects and cookies are in auth, so losing NATIVE's X-Forwarded-Proto/Host handling elsewhere is safe. The gateway was already pinned to none. ADR 0002 lines 46-49 and both env docs match the code at a04ad610. Round-2 findings: minor 1 (Forwarded: for=) resolved. Minor 2 (filter registered regardless of strategy) resolved. Nit 3 (customizers skipped) resolved. Nit 4 (no context test) partly resolved, see nit 1. Nit 5 (other servlet services on NATIVE) resolved by the Helm default. Nit 6 (techdebt pointer) still open. Security round-2 minors resolved: Forwarded header, dispatcher types plus customizers, and AuditInterceptor services now pinned to none. I found no regressions. Verification: forge-verify PASS at a04ad610 (293 tests, 0 skipped, 0 failures). evidence.md notes the outputs probably came from the Gradle cache, which is keyed on inputs. No blocker or major findings and all ACs met: approve.
